Strange Rules, Good Reasons

A Every job has rules. Most of us have to arrive on time, and many of us can't use our phones in meetings. But some jobs have rules that sound very strange — until you hear the reasons for them.

B In London, you can't just buy a black taxi and start work. First, drivers have to pass a test called “the Knowledge”, which many people call the hardest taxi test in the world. They have to learn about 25,000 streets and thousands of places within six miles of the city centre. In the exams they can't use a map or satnav: the examiner names two places, and the driver has to describe the best route from memory. Most people need three or four years to pass. Scientists at University College London found that the hippocampus, the part of the brain that remembers places, grew in the trainees who passed.

C Life on the International Space Station has rules too. Astronauts have to exercise for about two hours every day, because in space their muscles and bones get weaker. They can't have a shower — the water would float around the station — so they wash with wet towels and a special shampoo that they don't have to wash out. And they don't have to do any laundry, because there isn't a washing machine. They wear their clothes for a few days and then throw them away.

D Outside Buckingham Palace in London, the soldiers of the King's Guard wear red jackets and tall black fur hats called bearskins. Tourists love taking photos of them, but the guards are working: they can't chat with visitors or pose for photos. They have to stand still and look straight ahead. If someone comes too close, however, a guard can shout a loud warning.

E On many airlines, the captain and the co-pilot have to eat different meals: if one meal makes one pilot ill, the other can still fly. In the USA, pilots mustn't drink alcohol for eight hours before a flight, and international airline pilots have to stop flying at 65.

F Strange? Perhaps. But each rule has a reason: safety, health or good service. So next time you have to wear a uniform, think of the guard in the fur hat — at least you can talk to people!

Grammar · must / have to / can

TUSHUNTIRISH — MUST / HAVE TO / CAN

A have to = kerak, zarur (qoida bor yoki vaziyat shuni talab qiladi). Astronauts have to exercise every day. · My sister has to start work at six. Soʻroq va inkor do / does bilan: Do you have to wear a uniform? · He doesn't have to work at weekends. Oʻtgan zamon: had to — Yesterday I had to stay late.

B must = kerak, zarur — koʻpincha yozma qoida yoki gapiruvchining oʻz fikri. All visitors must wear a helmet. · I must call my mum tonight. must dan keyin to qoʻyilmaydi: must wear — must to wear emas. must ning oʻtgan zamon shakli yoʻq: had to ishlating.

C mustn't / can't = mumkin emas, ruxsat yoʻq. Pilots mustn't drink alcohol before a flight. · You can't use satnav in the test. can = mumkin, ruxsat bor: You can leave early on Friday.

D Tuzoq: mustn't ≠ don't have to. You mustn't come in — kirish mumkin emas, kirmang! You don't have to come in — kirish shart emas, lekin xohlasangiz kirishingiz mumkin. Astronauts don't have to do laundry — kir yuvish mashinasi yoʻq; ular qoidani buzmayapti.

DIQQAT — KOʻP UCHRAYDIGAN XATOLAR

1 ✗ I must to go now. → ✓ I must go now. — must dan keyin to yoʻq.

2 ✗ He have to work on Saturday. → ✓ He has to work on Saturday. — he / she / it + has to.

3 ✗ Do I must wear a tie? → ✓ Do I have to wear a tie? — soʻroq: do + have to.

4 ✗ Yesterday I must stay late. → ✓ Yesterday I had to stay late. — oʻtgan zamon = had to.

5 ✗ It's Sunday — you mustn't go to work. → ✓ you don't have to go to work. — shart emas, taqiqlanmagan.

Everyday English · offers, suggestions and reassurance

TUSHUNTIRISH — TAKLIF, MASLAHAT VA TASALLI

A Taklif (offer) — buni siz qilasiz: I'll do it, if you want. · Shall I help you? · Would you like me to …? · Do you want me to …? · Why don't I …? Istisno: taklifda Shall I …? ishlatiladi, hech qachon Will I …? emas.

B Maslahat (suggestion) — buni boshqa odam qilishi mumkin: Why don't you …? · You could … · Maybe you should … How about dan keyin -ing: How about taking her some flowers? — How about to take emas.

C Tasalli (reassurance) — odamga xavotir olmaslikni aytish: It doesn't matter. · Never mind. · Don't worry about it. · It's no problem. · I'll be fine.

D Taklifga javob: That would be great. · OK, if you're sure. · Are you sure? — No, don't worry. I'll do it tomorrow.

MODEL — AN OPINION TEXT

Should people who work at weekends earn more money?

Many people have to work at weekends — doctors, shop assistants, taxi drivers. In my opinion, they should earn more money for it.

Firstly, they miss time with their families. My cousin is a nurse, and she has to work two Saturdays a month, so she often misses family celebrations. Secondly, the rest of us need them: without them, we couldn't go shopping or see a doctor on Sunday.

Of course, some people like working at weekends. But I believe extra money is fair, because these workers give up something important.
